Every 'composes' value is the exit status of qnn-context-binary-generator --backend libQnnGpu.so on the physical board at 10.44.120.201; every failure line is copied verbatim from that run's log (inventory/logs/gpu_compose_logs.txt). Nothing here is inferred from documentation.

stock_gpu_op_package_datatypes._comment: From the SDK's own GPU op definition supplement (docs/QAIRT-Docs/QNN/OpDef/GpuOpDefSupplement.html), cross-checked against the compose logs above.
stock_gpu_op_package_datatypes.conclusion: the GPU backend's qti.aisw package is a float-only package: FLOAT_32 and FLOAT_16 for all 101 documented ops, with 8-bit fixed point accepted nowhere except as the input of Dequantize. The int8 gap is therefore not a handful of missing ops, it is the whole datatype.

op_package_dispatch._comment: Measured: how the GPU backend chooses which package serves a node.
op_package_dispatch.finding: dispatch is by Qnn_OpConfig_t::packageName, not by op type. Registering a package named 'flowc.gpu' that implements FullyConnected does not affect a DLC-composed node whose packageName is 'qti.aisw' -- the log still says 'OpPackage (qti.aisw) validation failure' and our validate() is never called. Registering the custom package *as* 'qti.aisw' is rejected: GPU_ERROR_OP_PACKAGE_FAILED(10023) - Duplicate operation name: FullyConnected.
op_package_dispatch.consequence: a DLC cannot be redirected to a custom op package. The route that works is the converter's C++ model output (qnn-onnx-converter -o model.cpp), whose per-node packageName string is rewritten before the model library is built. Everything measured here uses that route.
